items.title: Welcome, HSR-ER-HR705!
items.summary: The HR705 is a wheeled industrial humanoid from Huashu Robot designed for factory tasks like obstacle avoidance, sorting, and assembly. It stands 170 cm tall, weighs 200 kg, and features two 7-DOF collaborative arms. The platform uses Laser SLAM navigation and vision cameras for industrial space movement and object interaction. Although it supports specific tasks, its skill score of 3/10 indicates developing humanoid capability, with navigation rated lower than manipulation. The robot offers industrial connectivity via EtherCAT and Modbus, and is currently listed as a prototype.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, HSR-ER-HR705!". This report details the specifications and current status of the HR705, a wheeled industrial humanoid from Huashu Robot demonstrating developing humanoid capability. The robot stands at one hundred seventy centimeters tall and weighs two hundred kilograms, incorporating two seven-degrees-of-freedom collaborative arms for factory tasks such as obstacle avoidance, sorting, and assembly. The platform utilizes Laser SLAM navigation and vision cameras for industrial space movement and object interaction. Skill scoring indicates a development level of three out of ten, with navigation capabilities rated lower than manipulation skills. Furthermore, the robot offers industrial connectivity through EtherCAT and Modbus protocols and is currently cataloged as a prototype. This development signals ongoing progress in the integration of mobile robotics into industrial automation environments.

items.title: Audi humanoid robot trial targets parts sequencing in Ingolstadt
items.summary: Audi is testing wheeled humanoid robots at its Ingolstadt plant to pick and sequence vehicle parts. These robots use image recognition with two arms to handle variously shaped and packaged components from containers. The system is trained using real and simulated images to handle variations in parts effectively. The testing aims to validate the reliable performance of the sequencing task in a logistics setting. This project involves collaboration between Audi, Agile Robots, Dassault Systèmes, and NVIDIA to address automation challenges.

The project focuses on proving the feasibility of advanced robotic manipulation in complex industrial environments. This research indicates progress toward more robust and adaptable automation solutions in manufacturing and logistics.

items.title: Figure’s HQ Is Crawling With Figure 03 Robots. What Are They All Doing?
items.summary: Figure founder Brett Adcock shared videos showing dozens of Figure 03 robots roaming the campus, aiming for more robots than humans. The company has built its 1,000th Figure 03 but has disclosed only a few customer deployments, such as with BMW and Catalyst Brands. Most robots seen in the videos are engaged in non-task activities like walking or standing, rather than paid work. The robots are currently used for internal testing, data collection for Helix models, and experiments. This trend suggests Figure is moving toward a high density of robots on-site.

items.title: Robot integration brings high-precision production to midmarket manufacturers
items.summary: Robot integration makes high-precision manufacturing accessible to midmarket and smaller manufacturers. Robotic systems offer benefits like lower costs, easier programming, and enhanced capabilities through AI and sensors. These innovations enable manufacturers to improve efficiency, address labor shortages, and meet high quality demands. Real-world examples show robotics improving flexible production, part marking, throughput, and bin picking in various sectors. Consequently, robotic solutions drive sustainable growth for these manufacturers by making advanced precision viable.

items.title: Standing in the way of slop bowls: the woman blocking food delivery robots
items.summary: Carolyn Marvin protests food delivery robots to assert the public's right to have a say regarding their presence in public spaces. She blocks robots in Philadelphia to protest their incursion and to raise awareness about the issue. While some found her actions controversial, others supported her stance, arguing that robots pose hazards and affect jobs. The incident highlighted broader public skepticism toward AI and automation, leading to debates about the role of robots in public infrastructure. Marvin advocates for the necessity of public input in deciding where these technologies are allowed to operate.
items.audio_script: From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Standing in the way of slop bowls: the woman blocking food delivery robots". This report details a protest action taken by a woman to assert public input regarding the presence of food delivery robots in public spaces. The action occurred in Philadelphia where the individual physically obstructed the robots to raise awareness about the issue. Supporters argued that the robots presented hazards and impacted employment, while others viewed the actions as controversial. The incident reflected wider public skepticism concerning artificial intelligence and automation, prompting discussions about the role of these technologies in public infrastructure. The event underscores the need for public consultation in determining the operational parameters for robotics in public settings. This situation signals an ongoing debate regarding the integration and regulation of automated systems in communal environments.

items.title: Welcome, DH-5-6!
items.summary: The DH-5-6 dexterous hand received a Humanoid Guide Hand Score of 4 out of 10, placing it in the developing performance range. Its assessment includes a Degrees of Freedom rating of 2 out of 5 and a Strength rating of 2 out of 5, indicating balanced performance. Prospective buyers should consider application-specific evaluation rather than relying solely on the aggregate score for demanding manipulation tasks. Evaluation should focus on required movements and grip consequences before integration. The hand is manufactured by DH Robotics Technology Co., Ltd. and is listed at USD 4,000.

items.title: Welcome, Xiao Di!
items.summary: Xiao Di is BYD's first self-developed humanoid robot designed for customer interaction in car dealerships and various applications. Standing 161 cm and weighing 58.5 kg, it features a humanlike body with rounded joints and ten fingers. Its capabilities focus on obstacle avoidance, sorting goods, and product assembly, with navigation and manipulation rated as emerging platforms. The robot is a prototype priced at USD 25,000 and is being developed by BYD's embodied AI research team. It targets service, education, and industrial applications as an extension of the automaker's work beyond vehicles.

items.title: Welcome, Centaur G1!
items.summary: Centaur G1 is a wheeled humanoid robot from Elite Robots designed for precision manufacturing environments. It measures 150 cm tall, weighs 260 kg, and has 20 degrees of freedom across its structure, featuring two articulated arms and a mobile base. Key capabilities include obstacle avoidance and sorting goods, utilizing camera sensors for perception and SLAM navigation. The system integrates Elite Robots' collaborative robot technology with an embodied AI platform for control. The robot is listed as in production with a price of USD 48,000.

items.title: Welcome, Gino 1!
items.summary: Gino 1 is a 168 cm, 63 kg wheeled humanoid designed for warehouse environments. It features articulated arms with tactile hands for obstacle avoidance and sorting goods, and a maximum speed of 5.4 km/h. The robot utilizes NVIDIA Jetson Thor and the Geek+ Brain platform for its computing and control. Its assessed Humanoid.Guide Skill Score is low, focusing capabilities on warehouse sorting and obstacle avoidance. Launched in February 2026, the robot is available at a listed price of 55,000 USD.

items.title: Welcome, DexHand021 S!
items.summary: DexHand021 S is a compact, three-finger robotic hand manufactured by DexRobot, prioritizing affordability and low mass. It weighs 0.6 kg and has dimensions of 208 × 80 × 82.8 mm, positioning it as an entry-level option at a listed price of USD 1,000. Its performance scores place it in the developing category, with low ratings for both dexterity and strength. The design emphasizes a simpler physical format compared to five-finger hands. The product is currently in production, with further integration decisions depending on specific task requirements.

items.title: XPeng IRON walks off automated line, targets 2026 production
items.summary: XPeng's IRON humanoid has completed assembly and exited an automated production line, with mass production targeted for the end of 2026. The company claims over 80% of core manufacturing processes are automated, utilizing automotive-grade quality standards. The robot features 76 degrees of freedom and uses proprietary onboard AI chips for autonomous task execution. Funding supports a commercial rollout plan starting with internal deployments before a broader launch in 2027. XPeng expects higher gross margins on humanoid robots due to their technical complexity.

The company reports that over eighty percent of core manufacturing processes for the robot are automated, adhering to automotive-grade quality standards. The robot is equipped with seventy-six degrees of freedom and utilizes proprietary onboard artificial intelligence chips to execute autonomous tasks. This development indicates a tangible progression toward the commercialization of advanced humanoid robotics.
